The rules for partial fractions are summarized below.

alg_partial_fractionsApplying these rules, we find that: \[ {{CT:0}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{CT:1}}+\frac{C}{{CT:2}}\mbox{.}\]

Multiplying both sides through by {{CT:3}}

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:4}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} + {{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:4}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} + {{CT:9}} + {{CT:10}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\]

Matching coefficients

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:11}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:12}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:10}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\]

So

\[A={{CT:13}}\mbox{.}\]

Substituting this value in the other two equations we see that

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:14}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:15}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{.} \end{array}\]

Rearranging

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:16}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:17}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:18}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:19}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\] Multiplying the first of these two equations through by {{CT:20}} we obtain: \[ {{CT:21}}={{CT:22}}\mbox{,} \]

and subtracting the second of the pair of equations above from this equation we can eliminate C to give an equation only in B. We find that

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle B&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:23}}\mbox{,}\\ C&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:24}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\] Therefore \[{{CT:0}}={{CT:25}}.\]
